sections.overview:
1. 整体市场概况和情绪

今日主要事件：

  • Record Closes + Violent Four-Day Rebound: The S&P 500 closed at 7737, setting its first all-time high in two months, while the Dow broke above 54000 for the first time. SPY closed at 771.70 (+1.85%), QQQ at 721.17 (+3.01%), and IWM at 301.71 (+1.88%)—small caps rising in tandem indicates a broad-based rally rather than narrow concentration. The number the community kept repeating was that QQQ had gained about 10% over four trading days, even though last Wednesday felt like "the apocalypse." SOXL surged +15.45% in a single session, while INTC gained +7.61%.
  • AMD Beats on Both Lines but Plunges After Hours: Revenue came in at $11.54 billion (+50%), adjusted EPS at 1.66, data center revenue at $6.7 billion (+107%), and the midpoint of Q3 guidance at about $13 billion, all above expectations. However, capex was $808 million versus the expected $299 million. The stock fell more than 10% at one point after hours and was quoted at 479.57 at 19:41 (-0.92% versus Monday's close). It had reached an intraday high of 529.90—meaning it pulled back nearly 10% from the intraday peak but only fell back to "yesterday's price," which became the community's main point of contention tonight.
  • SpaceX's First Earnings Report + Musk Gives the Orders to Nvidia: Revenue reached $7.81 billion (+92%), beating expectations by nearly $1 billion, while losses were far smaller than expected. However, Q2 capex surged to $18.4 billion from $10.1 billion in the prior quarter, with $15.8 billion directed toward the AI business. On the earnings call, Musk announced that its AI data centers would exclusively use Nvidia, praised the Vera Rubin architecture, and said computing capacity would exceed 2GW by year-end and approach 10GW next year. He also discussed a "non-zero probability of $1 trillion in annual revenue" by 2029. NVDA traded at 213.48 after hours (+3.27%), while SPCX traded at 118.81 (+3.82%), with capital clearly rotating out of AMD and into NVDA.
  • The 8/6 Lock-Up Expiration Is This Week's Real Fuse: About 911.5 million shares—worth approximately $116 billion at the current price—will become tradable starting Thursday, while another 455.8 million shares will unlock under specified conditions. Musk and key insiders remain locked up until mid-2027. This is the bearish thesis with the strongest community consensus.
  • The Hormuz "Peace Trade" Is Once Again Just Hope: WTI fell more than 6% to $75.32 as the market priced in "navigation reopening soon," but actual negotiations remain stuck on passage fees—Iran wants 7%, while the U.S. is pushing for 5%. The 60-day free-passage window is expected to expire around mid-August. PLTR closed at 162.75 (+29.28%) following yesterday's earnings report, providing the strongest hard evidence yet for the current AI demand narrative.
